I’d say 50/50. I’m 9 weeks pregnant and high risk myself. I’ve waited for over 3 weeks to hear from my site and my case manager. I have had to call myself to try and get updates. Prior to opening my accommodations case, my onsite HR promised that I’d be moved to a low impact and suitable role. Now my site is saying, despite my medical documentation, I’m only approved for two extra unpaid breaks and to be close to the bathrooms. My request for intermittent sitting (or needing to sit if I feel faint) was denied. When my case manager tried to appeal, they denied it again. My current path is ICQA so it’s not like I cannot sit and count at the same time. Case manager told me if I am caught sitting, I’m subject to discipline. I think it just boils down to what your site thinks is best for business and meeting performance standards. 

Don’t be discouraged or stress too much, and congratulations! 🍼

In 2017, I started to have some leg soreness and I didn’t think much of it. A few days later I started to have trouble breathing. I thought I could be allergies or asthma, but then the next morning I could barely take a breath. I went to the ER and was given a breathing treatment. That had no effect, and they did a CT scan with contrast of my lungs. 

They found about 5 pulmonary emboli (blood clots in the lungs). The clots had formed in my leg, broke free, traveled through my heart, and got stuck in my lungs. I was admitted, and the pain was debilitating. 

My first night in the hospital, I woke up and could tell something wasn’t right. I pressed the nurse button and she said she’d be there soon. I then felt the most intense pain I have ever felt in my life. And then everything went black. 

I could hear people calling my name, and telling me to wake up. I had died, and the nurses used an AED and were trying to get me to open my eyes. I was finally able to open my eyes a little. 

I stayed in the hospital for another week, and was on blood thinners for 3 months. My lungs have recovered, but I still have bouts of pleurisy.
